summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with high CGM coverage (98.7 percent, 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, largest gap 65 minutes). Overall glucose average 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0 percent, coefficient of variation 32.6 percent, time above range 8.9 percent, time below range 5.1 percent. The daily shape in local time is consistent: a clean and flat fasting-like window from 04:00 to 09:00, a slow rise from 09:00 peaking at 16:00 (average 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range, 0.0 percent below range), then a decline into 18:00 and 19:00 (7.7 and 15.3 percent below range) and a second below-range band from 22:00 to 01:00 (up to 18.5 percent at 01:00). No carbohydrates were entered during the whole period (0 carb entries, 0.0 g total, no extended carb entries, COB reported as 0 in every sampled loop status), so all meal-related insulin was delivered reactively by UAM and temp basal. Manual boluses are very small (median 0.2 U, range 0.05 to 2.4 U) and cannot explain the observed excursions in either direction. The automation envelope is permissive: SMB permitted on every loop cycle, dynamic sensitivity compressing effective sensitivity to 27.8 to 54 mg/dL/U at high glucose with high insulin on board, observed insulin on board peaks of 4.73 and 5.94 U, and a maximum insulin on board allowance of 25 U that never engaged.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data are complete enough for segment-level analysis: 3995 valid entries, 0 invalid, 0 duplicates, 5-minute cadence, 98.7 percent coverage, 10 gaps with the largest 65 minutes, period 2026-08-07 21:15 to 2026-08-21 21:09 UTC. The local timezone is BST at UTC plus 60 minutes and hourly_glucose_local is the UTC series shifted by one hour, so all time-of-day statements use local hours. The 2026-08-07 daily row holds only 33 readings and was excluded from daily trend reasoning. The profile is complete: all 17 profile inventory rows carry values, and the scheduled basal sums to 16.2 U per day, matching the profile switch note recorded on 2026-08-13. Carb ratio values quoted inside loop reason strings match the profile carb ratio segments after local-time conversion, which independently confirms that the selected profile was active during the period. Telemetry completeness is the weak point: no carbohydrate data at all, and only 24 of 6214 device statuses and 40 of 2315 treatments are included as representative samples. Regime changes inside the window include a profile switch on 08-13, site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, an occlusion and pump error on 08-19, and GLP-1 1.25 mg notes on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20. The reason strings show a non-stock build with UAM Boost, prTrial, antBackout and twin fields, so some setting semantics may differ from documented behaviour.

analysis_steps.findings: Time in range 86.0 percent and coefficient of variation 32.6 percent meet common consensus targets, but time below range at 5.1 percent exceeds the usual 4 percent guideline and includes level-2 events. Two multi-reading clusters below 54 mg/dL are documented: 08-13 around 18:00 to 18:15 local (51, 47, 42, 45) and 08-14 around 19:05 to 19:15 local (48, 41, 41), plus an isolated 42 on 08-21 at 07:19 local shortly before a sensor change. Severe hyperglycemia clusters occurred on 08-15 around 17:30 local (286 to 293) and 08-18 around 13:00 local (285 to 290). Hypoglycemia is time-clustered rather than random: highest below-range hours are 01:00 (18.5 percent), 19:00 (15.3 percent), 00:00 (11.4 percent), 23:00 and 02:00 (10.1 percent) and 03:00 (10.2 percent), while 04:00 to 09:00 is essentially free of lows. Both level-2 clusters follow high-glucose automation responses by two to five hours. Sampled loop statuses show insulin on board peaks of 4.73 U (08-19, glucose 262) and 5.935 U (08-21, glucose 245.7) with effective sensitivity compressed to 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U and rates of 3.24 to 4 U/h. The last record of the window has no follow-up data, so that episode outcome is unobserved.

analysis_steps.findings: The only true fasting-like window, 04:00 to 09:00 local, is flat and in range (averages 106.0, 104.2, 99.5, 99.5, 110.5 mg/dL with below-range falling from 3.0 to 0.0 percent) even though it carries the highest scheduled basal of the day at 0.7 and 0.8 U/h. This supports the early-morning basal segments as they stand. From 10:00 to 16:00 glucose is persistently elevated with the daily peak at 16:00 (162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range) coinciding with the lowest basal segment of 0.5 U/h, then falls sharply into 18:00 and 19:00 where the two level-2 clusters occurred. Two explanations remain unseparated: an afternoon basal shortfall, or unannounced afternoon meals answered late and too strongly by automation followed by a delayed insulin tail. The second is favoured because the 08-14 window shows a fall from 234 to 56 mg/dL in 120 minutes after only about 1.3 U of manual insulin, a magnitude no 0.1 to 0.2 U/h basal difference can produce. GLP-1 dosing on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 is a third plausible contributor to delayed absorption and the worst days coincide with it. A separate unresolved observation is that sampled working targets include 80, 84, 86 and 87 mg/dL while the profile specifies 90 and 100 and both autosens target-adjustment switches are false; documented temporary targets explain the high values of 108 and 135 but not the low ones.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios were never exercised: zero carb entries and COB reported as 0 in every sampled status, so no carb ratio segment can be supported or refuted and all five remain unchanged. ISF is a single flat segment of 56 mg/dL/U, consistent with the profile name recorded on 08-13. Because dynamic sensitivity is enabled and autosens is disabled, the loop never used 56 for its own dosing; observed effective sensitivity ranged from 124 mg/dL/U at low glucose with low insulin on board down to 27.8 mg/dL/U at high glucose with high insulin on board, roughly twice as aggressive as the profile value in exactly the state that precedes the documented hypoglycemia clusters. A plausibility check on ISF 56 depends on total daily dose: the treatment summary shows 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U at an average of 0.42 U per entry, while basal appears separately as temp basal rate events, which suggests the figure is bolus and SMB only, giving roughly 36 U per day with the 16.2 U scheduled basal and making ISF 56 defensible. This inference is unlabelled in the package and is therefore held at medium confidence, but it lowers the priority of any profile ISF change. DIA is 10 hours with a free-peak insulin model; therapy response windows repeatedly show meaningful change still occurring at 240 and 360 minutes, so a long tail is observationally supported and DIA is not evidently too long. These tails are confounded by concurrent temp basal delivery and cannot be isolated.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and are the only mechanism delivering meal-responsive insulin, since no carbohydrates were ever entered. Among the activation conditions, smb_always_enabled true functionally overrides smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false, which are inert while no carbohydrates are logged; this is an internal inconsistency but not a safety concern today. The live interaction is smb_with_temp_target_enabled true with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false: the user set 135 mg/dL temporary targets repeatedly, twice for 180 minutes on 08-17 and 08-18, falling in the highest above-range afternoon hours, which suppresses SMB in that block. On 08-18 the 290 mg/dL peak occurred before the temporary target was set, so the target followed the excursion rather than causing it, and it plausibly functions as a deliberate guard against the 18:00 to 19:00 crash. On delivery settings, an SMB interval of 3 minutes against a 5-minute CGM cadence never throttles anything, max_smb_basal_minutes of 15 is inert on the unused COB path, and max_uam_smb_basal_minutes of 20 against a 0.5 to 0.8 U/h basal implies a UAM SMB ceiling near 0.17 to 0.27 U. Observed SMB sizes exceed that: 0.4 U where standardMaxBolus was 0.2 U on 08-07, and 1.6 U under a UAM High Boost on 08-19 at glucose 262 with insulin on board 4.73 U. The boost multipliers are not exposed in the package, so the minute-based caps have weaker authority over real delivery than the inventory implies and tightening them may achieve less than expected.

analysis_steps.findings: The sensitivity configuration is internally consistent: autosens disabled, dynamic sensitivity enabled, both autosens target-adjustment switches false, so autosens and dynamic ISF are not stacked. Reported sensitivity_ratio values of 1, 0.98, 0.94, 0.92, 0.91, 0.88 and 0.79 are the current neutral to resistance-direction output of the dynamic model and are not evidence about the autosens switch. The dynamic ISF adjustment factor of 70 percent produces the observed four-fold spread of effective sensitivity, aggressive precisely at high glucose with high insulin on board. On safety limits, max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 U/h is inert: the operative ceiling is roughly 4 U/h produced by the default multipliers, confirmed by the 08-14 log line stating the required rate was reduced to maxSafeBasal 4. That 4 U/h ceiling is still five to eight times the profile basal for those hours. max_iob_units of 25 U is 70 to 125 percent of the estimated total daily dose and never engaged as a brake, since observed peaks were 4.73 and 5.94 U. Honest limitation: because it never bound, lowering the maximum insulin on board would not by itself have prevented the 08-13 or 08-14 clusters, where insulin on board was around 1.4 to 1.6 U; it is a tail-risk guardrail rather than the fix for the observed pattern. The carbohydrate absorption settings, min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7, are wholly inert while COB stays 0 and become active the moment carbohydrate entry begins. Overall the automation is not primarily compensating for a defective static profile; a permissive envelope reacts strongly to unannounced rises and then produces delayed lows.

analysis_steps.findings: The user declaration in aaps_profile.analysis_context is present and timestamped 2026-08-21T21:08:10Z, with meal_strategies as an empty list, period_exceptions null and strategy_stable_for_period null. Because strategy_stable_for_period is not true, no representative period declaration can be derived, and no prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage or e-carb fields exist anywhere in the package to reproduce. Declared strategy and observed execution agree: no meal announcement, no prebolus and an effective immediate bolus percentage of zero. All 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses with is_extended_carbs false, doses distributed as 0.05 U six times, 0.1, 0.15 three times, 0.2 seven times, 0.25 twice, 0.3, 0.35, 0.45, 0.65 and a single 2.4 U given at glucose 181. At the profile carb ratios a 0.2 U dose covers only 2 to 3 g, and at ISF 56 it moves glucose about 11 mg/dL, so manual dosing cannot explain any observed excursion: on 08-17 a 0.05 U dose at glucose 125 was followed by 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes, and on 08-10 a 0.05 U dose at 93 was followed by 69 at 180 and 240 minutes. Three windows show a small dose just before a large unopposed rise (08-14 100 to 235 at 240 minutes, 08-19 164 to 205 at 60 minutes, 08-20 123 to 174 at 360 minutes), consistent with reactive rather than anticipatory dosing. Fifteen of the 23 windows with six-hour data are net negative at 360 minutes, several ending below 80 from a normal start, which is the signature of late-arriving insulin acting on the back end.

analysis_steps.findings: No extended carbohydrate data exist: extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is null, carb_treatment_entries is an empty list, and is_extended_carbs is false in all 24 response windows. No e-carb amount, start offset or duration can therefore be assessed and none is proposed, and no duration is inferred from any aggregate average. What can be said without inventing composition is that the afternoon block has the observational shape that a slow-absorption approach is designed for: a monotonic climb across 13:00 to 16:00 local peaking three or more hours after a plausible midday meal, then a decline into the 18:00 and 19:00 below-range band. A single reactive UAM response cannot match that curve because it starts late and then over-delivers into the tail. E-carbs in AAPS are a carbohydrate announcement spread over time that changes COB and the absorption model; they deliver no insulin themselves and are not a pump extended bolus, and nothing in this package supports discussing an extended bolus. A live safety dependency exists: min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7 are inert only while COB is 0, and combined with DIA 10 hours a long e-carb duration could sustain dosing into the 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 01:00 windows that already carry 7.7 to 18.5 percent below range. GLP-1 notes on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 indicate delayed gastric emptying, which makes absorption timing less stable across days and lowers confidence in any fixed duration.

analysis_steps.findings: The competing explanations resolve in favour of a permissive automation envelope acting on unannounced meals rather than a defective static profile. Three lines of evidence separate them. First, the only fasting-like window (04:00 to 09:00 local) is flat and in range at the highest scheduled basal of the day, which argues against systematic basal error. Second, manual boluses are far too small to explain any excursion, so the large falls are produced by SMB and temp basal. Third, effective sensitivity compresses to 27.8 to 54 mg/dL/U exactly at high glucose with high insulin on board, and SMB is permitted on every 5-minute cycle with boost logic exceeding the configured minute caps, which explains a peak at 16:00 followed by a crash at 18:00 to 19:00 as one oscillation rather than two independent problems. The afternoon basal segment at 0.5 U/h is the most eye-catching candidate but raising it would add insulin into the block that already ends with two level-2 clusters, so it is deliberately withheld. Profile ISF 56 is defensible against an estimated 36 U per day total daily dose and is in any case bypassed by dynamic sensitivity for loop dosing, so the correction lever belongs on the adjustment factor rather than on the profile. DIA 10 hours is observationally supported by real 240 to 360 minute action. Carb ratios cannot be judged at all. The single highest-value action is therefore reducing the dynamic ISF adjustment factor, which directly weakens the aggressive high-glucose dosing that precedes every documented cluster, with the explicit and unavoidable trade-off that it also weakens correction in the 10:00 to 17:00 above-range band. Two unresolved items must not be silently resolved: the source of working targets of 80 to 87 mg/dL where the profile states 90 and 100 with both autosens target switches false, and how much of the 00:00 to 03:00 below-range band is genuine rather than sensor artefact near the 08-21 sensor change.

strengths: CGM data quality is excellent and supports segment-level analysis: 98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, no invalid or duplicate entries and a largest gap of only 65 minutes.
Overall control is good by consensus measures despite no carbohydrate announcement at all: time in range 86.0 percent, coefficient of variation 32.6 percent and average glucose 121.6 mg/dL.

The fasting-like window from 04:00 to 09:00 local is flat and in range (99.5 to 110.5 mg/dL with 0.0 to 3.0 percent below range) at the highest scheduled basal of the day, which is strong evidence that the early-morning basal segments are well matched.
Manual correction sizing is conservative and appropriate: a median dose of 0.2 U moves glucose about 11 mg/dL at the profile ISF, so user-initiated dosing is not contributing to the observed lows.

The sensitivity configuration is internally consistent, with autosens disabled while dynamic sensitivity is enabled and both autosens target-adjustment switches off, so two sensitivity systems are not stacked.

The profile is complete and verifiably active: all 17 profile rows carry values, the scheduled basal of 16.2 U per day matches the profile switch note on 08-13, and carb ratios quoted in loop reason strings match the profile segments after local-time conversion.
Several recent days show strong stability, including 08-20 with 90.6 percent in range and only 1.0 percent below range, and 08-09 with 96.5 percent in range.
issues: Time below range of 5.1 percent exceeds the usual 4 percent guideline and includes two documented level-2 clusters: 08-13 around 18:00 to 18:15 local (51, 47, 42, 45 mg/dL) and 08-14 around 19:05 to 19:15 local (48, 41, 41 mg/dL). Lows are concentrated at 19:00 (15.3 percent) and 22:00 to 01:00 (up to 18.5 percent at 01:00), and both clusters follow high-glucose automation responses by two to five hours.

Effective sensitivity is roughly twice the profile value at high glucose. With dynamic sensitivity enabled and an adjustment factor of 70 percent, observed effective sensitivity ranged from 124 mg/dL/U at low glucose down to 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U at glucose 262 and 245.7 with insulin on board of 4.73 and 5.94 U, against a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U. The aggressive half of that range operates exactly in the state preceding the documented clusters.

An afternoon oscillation runs between the daily peak and the deepest daytime low. Glucose climbs monotonically from 09:00 to a peak of 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 local with 32.1 percent above range and 0.0 percent below range, then falls into 7.7 percent below range at 18:00 and 15.3 percent at 19:00. Peak and crash are three hours apart in the same block and behave as one oscillation, not two independent problems.

Insulin on board accumulates without an effective configured brake. Observed peaks were 4.73 and 5.94 U, roughly 16 to 30 percent of an estimated 36 U total daily dose, accumulated within single episodes and combined with a 10-hour DIA. The configured maximum of 25 U never engaged, and the operative basal ceiling is about 4 U/h from default multipliers rather than the 12 U/h setting, which is inert.

SMB delivery caps have weaker authority than the settings imply. max_uam_smb_basal_minutes of 20 against a 0.5 to 0.8 U/h basal implies a UAM SMB ceiling near 0.17 to 0.27 U, yet observed SMB sizes were 0.4 U where standardMaxBolus was 0.2 U and 1.6 U under a UAM High Boost. The boost multipliers are not exposed in the package, so tightening the minute caps may achieve less than expected.

Working targets below the profile values are unexplained. Sampled loop statuses report working targets of 80, 84, 86 and 87 mg/dL while the profile specifies 90 and 100 mg/dL and both autosens target-adjustment switches are false. Documented temporary targets explain the values of 108 and 135 but not the low ones. No inventory setting in the package accounts for this, and it interacts directly with the evening and overnight below-range bands.

No carbohydrate data of any kind exist, so meal-related parameters are untestable. The period contains 0 carb entries, 0.0 g total carbohydrate, no extended carb entries and COB reported as 0 in every sampled loop status. All five carb ratio segments and both carbohydrate absorption settings are consequently unexercised, and no e-carb amount, offset or duration can be assessed.

Several confounders limit attribution. GLP-1 1.25 mg notes on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 indicate delayed gastric emptying on the worst days for both above and below range, an occlusion and pump error occurred on 08-19, and the isolated 42 mg/dL on 08-21 at 07:19 local precedes a sensor change and may be artefact. No hypoglycemia treatments are logged despite rebound patterns implying unlogged rescue carbohydrate.

recommendations.title: Primary: reduce the dynamic ISF adjustment factor as the single first change
recommendations.description: This is the one lever that acts directly on the mechanism linking every documented hypoglycemia cluster to a preceding high. Effective sensitivity compresses from 124 mg/dL/U at low glucose to 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U at glucose 262 and 245.7 with insulin on board of 4.73 and 5.94 U, roughly twice as aggressive as the flat profile ISF of 56. Both level-2 clusters on 08-13 and 08-14 followed high-glucose automation responses by two to five hours, and manual boluses in those windows were only 0.2 to 1.3 U, far too small to explain falls of 125 to 178 mg/dL. The trade-off is stated plainly and is not hidden: a single global factor acts in opposite directions on the two problems, so reducing it also weakens correction in the 10:00 to 17:00 above-range band where time above range reaches 32.1 percent at 16:00. Whether 5.1 percent below range with two level-2 clusters outranks 8.9 percent above range is a care-team judgement, not a data-only conclusion. Confidence is medium because the build applies undocumented boost and dosing-sensitivity layers on top of this factor.

suggested_change.primary_metric: time below range in local hours 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 01:00
suggested_change.counter_metric: time above range in local hours 10:00 to 17:00
suggested_change.stop_condition: any increase in level-2 events or any sustained rise above range beyond the pre-change afternoon pattern

recommendations.title: Second: lower the maximum insulin on board as an independent tail-risk guardrail
recommendations.description: Included because it changes the safe action order rather than because it fixes the observed pattern. The configured maximum of 25 U is 70 to 125 percent of an estimated 36 U total daily dose and never engaged in 14 days, since observed peaks were 4.73 and 5.94 U. It therefore would not by itself have prevented the 08-13 or 08-14 clusters, where insulin on board was only about 1.4 to 1.6 U. Its value is that it places a numeric ceiling on accumulation during prolonged highs, a state currently bounded only by behaviour: the final record of the window shows insulin on board 5.935 U at glucose 245.7 with a requested 2.12 U and a 4 U/h rate, and no follow-up data exist for that episode. Because it rarely binds, it interferes minimally with the primary change, but it must still occupy its own observation window.

suggested_change.rationale_note: provides clear headroom above the observed working maximum of 5.94 U while ending the unbounded allowance
suggested_change.depends_on: confirmation that 275.95 U over 14 days is bolus and SMB only, which determines total daily dose

recommendations.title: Third: begin carbohydrate logging for one recurring meal as a diagnostic, not a setting change
recommendations.description: With 0 carb entries and COB reported as 0 throughout, carb ratios cannot be evaluated, no e-carb parameter can be assessed, and the afternoon peak cannot be separated from a possible basal shortfall. Logging the midday or afternoon meal at eating time with an approximate gram estimate, changing nothing else, is the single action that unblocks the most downstream analysis. It is listed third because it is not risk-free: entering carbohydrate activates COB and therefore activates min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7, which are inert today, so it changes loop behaviour and must occupy its own observation window after the automation changes have settled.

suggested_change.action: log carbohydrates for one recurring meal for 7 consecutive days
unblocks: separation of meal effect from afternoon basal

recommendations.title: Fourth: clarify the source of working targets below the profile values before any target edit
recommendations.description: Sampled statuses show working targets of 80, 84, 86 and 87 mg/dL while the profile specifies 90 and 100 and both autosens target-adjustment switches are false. Documented temporary targets account for 108 and 135 but not the low values, and no setting in the decision inventory explains them. This changes the safe action order: editing a profile target without understanding an active override could deepen the evening and overnight below-range bands that already reach 15.3 and 18.5 percent. This is a clarification step, not a parameter change.

suggested_change.action: clarify with the care team or build documentation which mechanism lowers the working target below the profile value

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all 17 profile rows unchanged for now, including the eye-catching 0.5 U/h afternoon basal segment at 16:00, and make the first change on the automation side instead by reducing the dynamic ISF adjustment factor.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The most tempting profile change is raising profile.basal.16_00 from 0.5 U/h, because the lowest basal segment of the day aligns with the daily peak of 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 local. It is deliberately withheld because the same block ends in the deepest daytime lows, 7.7 percent below range at 18:00 and 15.3 percent at 19:00, containing both documented level-2 clusters, so added basal would flow directly into an episode that already finishes too low. Three findings support keeping the profile: the only fasting-like window, 04:00 to 09:00 local, is flat and in range at the highest scheduled basal of the day, which argues against systematic basal error; manual boluses of 0.05 to 1.3 U cannot explain falls of 125 to 178 mg/dL, so those falls come from SMB and temp basal rather than from profile settings; and profile ISF 56 is both defensible against an estimated 36 U per day total daily dose and bypassed by dynamic sensitivity for loop dosing, which moves the correction lever off the profile entirely. DIA 10 hours is observationally supported by real glucose change still occurring at 240 to 360 minutes, and all five carb ratios are untestable with zero carbohydrate entries. Confidence is low because meals, corrections and GLP-1 effects on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 remain plausible alternative explanations for the afternoon shape that the current data cannot separate.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After the dynamic ISF adjustment factor change has run for at least 10 days, re-examine the local 16:00 hour specifically: if average glucose there remains at or above roughly 160 mg/dL with time above range near 32 percent while time below range at 18:00 and 19:00 has fallen below about 4 percent, then raising profile.basal.16_00 from 0.5 U/h by one small step becomes supportable as the next single change; if the 18:00 to 19:00 lows persist, keep the basal unchanged and look again at meal timing instead.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local hours 00:00 to 03:00 show below-range of 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent, which looks like overnight basal excess, but hour 04:00 improves to 3.0 percent below range, so lows sit in the first half of the night only. That shape points to carry-over insulin on board from evening dosing under a 10-hour DIA rather than a flat basal error. Uncertainty: part of this band may be sensor artefact, and the isolated 42 mg/dL on 08-21 at 07:19 local precedes a sensor change. Dependencies: the evening automation change must be observed first, since it directly feeds this window.

Evidence: local hour 05:00 averages 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent in range and 4.8 percent below range, and hour 06:00 averages 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 percent in range. This is part of the cleanest fasting-like window in the dataset and gives no support for a change. Uncertainty: no dedicated basal test exists to confirm this independently of overnight insulin on board. Dependencies: none blocking.

Evidence: this is the highest scheduled basal of the day and it produces the best glycemia in the dataset, with local hours 06:00 to 09:00 averaging 99.5, 99.5, 110.5 and 132.9 mg/dL and below-range falling from 2.5 to 0.0 percent. Uncertainty: the rise beginning at 09:00 could indicate an early shortfall, but with zero carbohydrate entries an unannounced breakfast is at least as plausible. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging would separate these two explanations.

Evidence: local hours 10:00 to 15:00 are persistently elevated at 148.0, 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1 and 153.0 mg/dL with time above range from 7.5 to 26.3 percent, which could suggest under-basalisation. Change is withheld because COB was 0 in every sampled status and no carbohydrates were entered, so unannounced meals answered late by UAM remain an equally plausible explanation. Uncertainty: high, the two explanations are not separable with current data. Dependencies: resolution requires carbohydrate logging, and any increase must wait until the 18:00 to 19:00 below-range band is stable.

Evidence: this is the strongest apparent basal signal in the dataset and is deliberately withheld. The lowest basal segment of the day coincides with the daily peak at local 16:00 of 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent above range and 0.0 percent below range, which favours an increase, but the same block ends at 18:00 and 19:00 with 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range and contains both level-2 clusters on 08-13 and 08-14. The 08-14 fall from 234 to 56 mg/dL in 120 minutes after only about 1.3 U of manual insulin shows this window is dominated by automation, not by a 0.1 to 0.2 U/h basal difference. Uncertainty: GLP-1 dosing on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 is a third plausible contributor. Dependencies: revisit only after the dynamic ISF adjustment factor change has been observed.

Evidence: local hour 18:00 shows 7.7 percent below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, which could argue for a reduction, but the lows cluster on specific days, 08-13 and 08-14, rather than recurring evenly, so they read as the tail of afternoon automation dosing rather than a steady-state basal effect. Reducing basal would treat a symptom whose cause sits upstream. Uncertainty: a genuine small basal excess cannot be excluded. Dependencies: reassess only after the automation change, and never together with a change to the adjacent 16:00 or 19:00 segments.

Evidence: local hour 19:00 carries 15.3 percent below range with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, the second-worst below-range hour, and this is the highest evening basal segment, so a reduction is tempting. Change is withheld because both level-2 clusters in this hour occurred two to five hours after high-glucose automation responses, and on 08-17 a 0.05 U dose at glucose 125 was followed by 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes, a fall no 0.7 U/h basal segment can produce alone. Uncertainty: a contributory basal excess remains possible and this is the leading profile candidate if the automation change does not resolve the pattern. Dependencies: strictly after the dynamic ISF adjustment factor observation window.

Evidence: not exercised at any point in the period, with 0 carb entries, 0.0 g total carbohydrate and COB reported as 0 in every sampled loop status, so there is nothing supporting or refuting this value. Change is unsupported and the value is present, so it is kept rather than reported as missing. Uncertainty: complete, correctness is unknown rather than confirmed. Dependencies: only carbohydrate logging can unblock evaluation.

Evidence: not exercised, since no carbohydrates were entered in the period. The value does appear in a loop reason string at 04:01 local and matches the profile segment, which confirms that the selected profile was active with local-time boundaries but says nothing about correctness. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging.

Evidence: not exercised, with zero carbohydrate entries throughout. The value appears in reason strings at 09:11 local, matching the profile segment and confirming profile activity only. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging for the morning meal would be needed before any judgement.

Evidence: not exercised, with zero carbohydrate entries. This segment covers the highest above-range block of the day and is therefore the most likely future candidate for evaluation, but with no COB ever generated there is nothing to evaluate now. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: the recommended carbohydrate logging targets exactly this meal window.

Evidence: not exercised, with zero carbohydrate entries. The evening block does carry elevated below-range values from 22:00 to 01:00, but without any carbohydrate announcement that pattern is attributable to insulin tails rather than to a carb ratio. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging, and this meal should be evaluated last because of the existing overnight below-range band.

Evidence: an earlier working hypothesis that ISF 56 might be too aggressive is withdrawn here for two reasons. First, with dynamic sensitivity enabled and autosens disabled the loop never used 56 for its own dosing, since every sampled status quotes an effective sensitivity between 27.8 and 124 mg/dL/U, so the profile value governs the bolus calculator rather than closed-loop correction. Second, 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U at 0.42 U per entry, with basal appearing separately as temp basal rate events, indicates the figure is bolus and SMB only and implies roughly 36 U per day with the 16.2 U scheduled basal, making 56 defensible. Uncertainty: the insulin total is not explicitly labelled, so this inference is held at medium confidence. Dependencies: the correction lever belongs on the dynamic ISF adjustment factor instead, and these two must never be changed together.

Evidence: a higher overnight target would be a plausible response to 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range in local hours 22:00 to 01:00, but sampled statuses report working targets of 80, 84, 86 and 87 mg/dL while the profile states 90 and both autosens target-adjustment switches are false, so an unidentified mechanism is already overriding the profile value and editing the profile number may not produce the intended effect. Uncertainty: high, and part of this below-range band may be sensor artefact. Dependencies: blocked pending clarification of the target override.

Evidence: the window covered by this target contains both the best block of the day, 04:00 to 09:00 local flat and in range, and the worst above-range block, 10:00 to 17:00, so no single target change would serve both. Lowering it would add risk to the 18:00 to 19:00 crash while raising it would worsen the afternoon peak. Uncertainty: the same unexplained working-target override applies, since values of 80 and 87 were observed against a profile value of 100. Dependencies: blocked pending clarification of the override.

Evidence: this segment begins the highest below-range band of the day and is a genuine future candidate, but it is kept because the effective working target is already lower than the profile value through an unidentified mechanism and no inventory setting in the package explains it. Uncertainty: high, and the artefact question for the 00:00 to 03:00 lows is unresolved. Dependencies: clarification of the target override, and it must not be changed alongside any basal or automation change.

Evidence: DIA 10 hours is long, but shortening it is unsupported and would likely be harmful, because therapy response windows repeatedly show real glucose change still occurring at 240 and 360 minutes, for example 08-19 with minus 161 mg/dL at 240 minutes and minus 176 at 360, and 08-17 with minus 68 and minus 50. A shorter DIA would under-report insulin on board and permit more stacking, the opposite of what the observed pattern needs. Uncertainty: these tails are confounded by concurrent temp basal delivery, so DIA cannot be isolated from automation dosing. Dependencies: DIA amplifies but does not cause the pattern, so the limits and the sensitivity factor are the operative levers.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted and the decision is keep. With 0 carb entries and COB reported as 0 throughout, UAM is the only mechanism delivering meal-responsive insulin, and time in range of 86.0 percent with a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent was achieved without any carbohydrate announcement. Disabling either switch would remove the response to the 09:00 to 16:00 rise and would very likely worsen the 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 without a compensating meal-announcement strategy. Uncertainty: low for this decision. Dependencies: the strength of the UAM response, not its existence, is the issue, and that is addressed through the sensitivity factor.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB activation conditions (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, smb_with_temp_target_enabled, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: all five components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted. smb_always_enabled true functionally overrides the two COB-linked switches, which are inert while no carbohydrates are logged, an internal inconsistency but not a safety concern today. The live interaction is smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false combined with repeated 135 mg/dL temporary targets, twice for 180 minutes on 08-17 and 08-18, which suppresses SMB during the highest above-range hours. Enabling it is explicitly not recommended, because it would inject SMB into the windows the user appears to be using as protection against the documented level-2 clusters, and on 08-18 the 290 mg/dL peak preceded the temporary target rather than resulting from it. Uncertainty: whether the temporary targets are a deliberate crash workaround is not confirmed in the package. Dependencies: re-evaluate after the sensitivity change and after carbohydrate logging begins.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB strength and frequency (smb_interval_minutes, max_smb_basal_minutes, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes)
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: all three components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted. An earlier working view treated this group as a change candidate and it is downgraded to keep, because these caps do not control actual delivery: max_uam_smb_basal_minutes of 20 against a 0.5 to 0.8 U/h basal implies a ceiling near 0.17 to 0.27 U, yet observed SMB sizes were 0.4 U where standardMaxBolus was 0.2 U and 1.6 U under a UAM High Boost, so the build-specific boost exceeds the configured cap. Tightening a cap that is already bypassed would give a false sense of control while consuming an observation window. The 3-minute interval also never throttles anything against a 5-minute CGM cadence. Uncertainty: the boost multipliers are not exposed in the package. Dependencies: reconsider only if the sensitivity factor change fails to reduce the evening below-range band, and only as a single isolated change.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits (max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted and change is used with supported old and new values. Only the insulin-on-board component changes. max_basal_u_per_hour stays at 12 U/h because it is inert, since the operative ceiling is about 4 U/h from the default multipliers, confirmed by the 08-14 log line reducing a required 5.9 U/h to maxSafeBasal 4, so editing it would change nothing observable. max_iob_units drops from 25 U to 8 U because 25 U is 70 to 125 percent of an estimated 36 U total daily dose and never engaged in 14 days, while the observed working maximum was 5.935 U on 08-21 at glucose 245.7 with a requested 2.12 U and a 4 U/h rate, an episode whose outcome is unobserved because the data window ends there. A value of 8 U leaves clear headroom above observed use while ending an effectively unbounded allowance. Stated honestly, because this limit never bound it would not by itself have prevented the 08-13 or 08-14 clusters, where insulin on board was only about 1.4 to 1.6 U, so it is a tail-risk guardrail rather than the fix for the observed pattern. Uncertainty: the total daily dose estimate rests on an unlabelled field and should be confirmed before applying. Dependencies: apply in its own observation window, never together with the sensitivity factor change.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / Autosens and Dynamic ISF (autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, autosens_raises_target, autosens_lowers_target, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: all five components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted. Only the adjustment factor changes, from 70 to 60 percent; the four switches stay as they are because the configuration is internally consistent, with autosens and dynamic sensitivity correctly not stacked and both target-adjustment switches off. The reported sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79 to 1.0 are the current neutral to resistance-direction output of the dynamic model and are not evidence about the autosens switch, so they do not justify enabling autosens. The factor is reduced because it produces the four-fold sensitivity spread that drives the observed pattern, from 124 mg/dL/U at low glucose down to 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U at glucose 262 and 245.7 with insulin on board of 4.73 and 5.94 U, roughly twice as aggressive as the profile ISF of 56 precisely in the state preceding both level-2 clusters. Trade-off stated plainly: this single global factor acts in opposite directions on the two problems, so it will also weaken correction in the 10:00 to 17:00 block where time above range reaches 32.1 percent, and the balance between 5.1 percent below range and 8.9 percent above range is a care-team judgement. Uncertainty: medium, because the build applies undocumented UAM Boost and dosing-sensitivity layers on top of this factor, so the realised effect may be smaller or larger than the factor change implies. Dependencies: this is the primary change and must run alone, never combined with the insulin-on-board limit, any basal segment, or profile ISF.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted. Both parameters act only on the COB and carbohydrate-absorption path, which was completely unexercised, with 0 carb entries, 0.0 g total, no extended carb entries and COB reported as 0 in all 24 sampled statuses, so no observation in this dataset can support or refute either value, and min_5m_carbimpact of 8 is a conventional setting. One forward-looking caution rather than a change: both become active the moment carbohydrate entry begins, and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 combined with DIA 10 hours could sustain dosing into the 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 01:00 windows that already carry 7.7 to 18.5 percent below range. Uncertainty: complete, since the path has never run. Dependencies: revisit only after carbohydrate logging has produced real absorption curves.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Announce before accelerating, and add nothing to the front of the meal yet. Today there is no prebolus, an effective immediate bolus percentage of zero, and every meal is answered reactively by SMB and UAM after the rise has already started, with a 10-hour insulin tail landing two to five hours later in the 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 01:00 below-range bands. Keep SMB and UAM enabled throughout, since they are the only meal mechanism in use. Do not introduce a prebolus, do not set an immediate bolus percentage, and do not start e-carbs at this stage. The single productive first step is to give the loop the input it has never had: log one recurring meal at eating time with an approximate carbohydrate estimate, changing nothing else, and only after the automation guardrails have settled. Prebolus timing, an immediate bolus percentage and any e-carb amount, offset or duration should be discussed only once that logged data exists.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user declaration in aaps_profile.analysis_context is present and timestamped but contains an empty meal_strategies list with period_exceptions null and strategy_stable_for_period null, so no prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage or e-carb fields exist in the package to reproduce, and none are invented. Declared strategy and observed execution agree, which is itself informative: telemetry shows 0 carb entries, 0.0 g total and COB 0 in every sampled status, and all 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses with is_extended_carbs false and a median dose of 0.2 U, which covers only 2 to 3 g at the profile carb ratios and moves glucose about 11 mg/dL at ISF 56. Manual dosing therefore cannot explain any observed excursion, as shown on 08-17 where 0.05 U at glucose 125 was followed by 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes. Fifteen of the 23 windows with six-hour data are net negative at 360 minutes, several ending below 80 from a normal start, which is the signature of late-arriving insulin acting on the back end. Adding front-loaded insulin to a pattern that already produces two level-2 clusters would increase risk before improving range.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: For 7 consecutive days, enter the midday or afternoon meal into AAPS at the moment eating starts with an approximate carbohydrate estimate, and change nothing else: no profile edit, no automation edit, no prebolus, no e-carbs. This single action unblocks carb ratio evaluation, produces the first real absorption curve that any e-carb discussion would require, and separates unannounced meals from an afternoon basal shortfall as the cause of the 16:00 peak. Note that it does change loop behaviour, because COB becomes live and activates min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours, so it must occupy its own observation window after the automation changes have settled.

exceptions.suggestion: Treat this as the highest-risk block for any front-loaded insulin: it is the best future candidate for a slow-absorption approach and the worst candidate for a prebolus. Change nothing here until the sensitivity factor change has been observed, and first establish whether the repeated 135 mg/dL temporary targets are a deliberate guard against the crash.
exceptions.rationale: This block holds the largest and slowest rise of the day, peaking at 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range and 0.0 percent below range, then falls within three hours to 7.7 percent below range at 18:00 and 15.3 percent at 19:00, containing both level-2 clusters on 08-13 and 08-14. The peak and the deepest daytime low are three hours apart in the same block, so meal parameters cannot be evaluated here while the automation envelope remains permissive. The user set 180-minute 135 mg/dL temporary targets inside this block on 08-17 and 08-18.

exceptions.pattern: Late-evening and overnight block, local 21:00 to 01:00
exceptions.suggestion: If a late meal is being eaten, consider it last for any future prebolus or immediate bolus percentage, not first, and avoid any e-carb duration that would extend dosing into the night.
exceptions.rationale: Glucose rises to 127.6 mg/dL at 22:00 then declines to 105.7, 93.3 and 90.6 with below-range of 10.1, 11.4 and 18.5 percent, the highest below-range hour in the dataset. The mechanism differs from the afternoon block: here the driver is a 10-hour insulin tail against a 90 mg/dL overnight target with observed working targets as low as 80 to 87, rather than late over-correction at high glucose. A competing explanation that part of this band is sensor artefact remains unresolved, which is a further reason not to act on it through meal parameters.

implementation_steps: Step 0, before any change: confirm with the care team whether the 275.95 U recorded across 655 insulin entries represents bolus and SMB only or all insulin delivery, since this determines whether the estimated total daily dose is about 36 or about 20 U per day and governs both the size of the insulin-on-board limit and whether profile ISF 56 remains defensible. Also clarify which mechanism produces working targets of 80 to 87 mg/dL when the profile states 90 and 100 and both autosens target-adjustment switches are false, because this blocks all target discussion.

Step 1, primary change, alone: reduce dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent from 70 to 60 and change nothing else. Observe for at least 10 days. The primary metric is time below range in local hours 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 01:00, currently 7.7, 15.3, 10.1, 11.4 and 18.5 percent. The counter-metric is time above range in local hours 10:00 to 17:00, currently 7.5 to 32.1 percent, which is expected to worsen somewhat. Stop and reconsider if any increase in level-2 events occurs or if glucose rises persistently beyond the pre-change afternoon pattern.

Step 2, separate window: reduce max_iob_units from 25 U to 8 U, keeping max_basal_u_per_hour at 12 U/h because it is inert against the operative 4 U/h ceiling. Observe for at least 7 days. Because the limit rarely binds, expect little day-to-day change; the objective is a numeric ceiling on accumulation during prolonged highs, and the check is whether any loop cycle is now limited by the new value at a moment when that limitation is unwelcome.

Step 3, separate window, diagnostic only: log one recurring meal, preferably the midday or afternoon meal, at eating time with an approximate carbohydrate estimate for 7 consecutive days, with no other change. Note that this activates the COB path and therefore min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours, which have been inert until now, so it does alter loop behaviour and must not share a window with any other change.

Step 4, review point only: after steps 1 to 3, re-examine local hour 16:00. If average glucose there remains at or above roughly 160 mg/dL with time above range near 32 percent while time below range at 18:00 and 19:00 has fallen below about 4 percent, then raising profile.basal.16_00 from 0.5 U/h by one small step becomes supportable as the next single change. If the 18:00 to 19:00 lows persist, keep the basal unchanged and examine meal timing instead.

Step 5, only if the evening below-range band persists after step 1: consider profile.basal.19_00 at 0.7 U/h as the leading remaining profile candidate, as a single isolated change, and never together with the adjacent 16:00 or 18:00 segments.
Throughout: apply one change per observation window, keep a written note of what changed and when, and bring the sequence and the observed metrics to the care team before proceeding to the next step.
education: Time in range of 86.0 percent and a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent both meet common consensus targets, while time below range of 5.1 percent exceeds the usual guideline of 4 percent. Two-sided metrics matter, because a good average of 121.6 mg/dL can coexist with a genuine hypoglycemia burden, and in this dataset the lows are concentrated in specific hours rather than spread evenly.

When dynamic sensitivity is enabled and autosens is disabled, the loop derives its working sensitivity from glucose and total daily dose rather than using the profile ISF directly. In this period the profile value of 56 mg/dL/U never appeared in a loop decision, and observed working values ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U. This is why the profile ISF row and the adjustment factor are separate levers and should not be adjusted together.

A reported sensitivity_ratio of 1 means the current adjustment is neutral, not that autosens is switched off or malfunctioning. Similarly, remaining time in an SMB waiting message is not the configured SMB interval, and UAM does not create duplicate carbohydrate counting; COB was 0 in this period simply because no carbohydrates were ever entered.

Not every configured limit is the limit that actually applies. Here max_basal_u_per_hour is 12 U/h, but the default safety multipliers produced an operative ceiling near 4 U/h, which the log confirms directly. Checking which constraint actually binds prevents changing a setting that cannot affect anything.

E-carbs in AAPS are a carbohydrate announcement spread over time. They deliver no insulin by themselves; they change the carbohydrate-on-board estimate and the absorption model so the loop can dose along the curve. This is different from a pump extended bolus, which delivers insulin over time without any carbohydrate model.

A long duration of insulin action does not by itself cause lows, but it changes when they appear. With a 10-hour setting and real glucose change still measurable 4 to 6 hours after dosing, insulin given late in response to a high tends to act after the rise has resolved, which is a common mechanism behind a mid-afternoon peak followed by an early-evening low.

GLP-1 medication slows gastric emptying, which can flatten and delay the glucose rise after eating and make absorption timing vary between days. Doses recorded on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 are a reason to interpret day-to-day differences cautiously rather than as changes in insulin requirements.

Changing one setting at a time is not merely procedural caution. Here the afternoon high and the early-evening low sit three hours apart in the same block, so two simultaneous changes would make it impossible to tell which one produced any observed effect, or in which direction.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice. TuneMyBG prepares data for review, and every proposed change must be independently verified with your diabetes care team before anything is altered.
No setting has been or will be changed automatically. Every item above is a proposal for discussion, and nothing here should be applied directly to AAPS without clinical review.

Make one change at a time, allow a full observation window before the next, and monitor glucose closely, with particular attention to the local hours 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 01:00 where time below range currently reaches 15.3 and 18.5 percent.

Two level-2 hypoglycemia clusters below 54 mg/dL are documented, on 08-13 around 18:00 to 18:15 local and on 08-14 around 19:05 to 19:15 local, with readings as low as 41 mg/dL. Discuss these events and your hypoglycemia treatment plan with your care team before making any change that could increase insulin delivery.

The primary proposal reduces correction strength at high glucose and is expected to increase time above range in the 10:00 to 17:00 block as a direct trade-off. Agree in advance with your care team what level of hyperglycemia is acceptable in exchange for reduced hypoglycemia, and what would trigger reverting the change.

Do not raise the afternoon basal segment, add a prebolus, enable SMB with high temporary targets, or start e-carbs at this stage, because each of these would add insulin into windows that already produce documented severe lows.

No hypoglycemia treatments were recorded in this period even though rebound patterns suggest rescue carbohydrate was taken. Logging lows and their treatment would materially improve the safety of any future analysis.

An occlusion and pump error were recorded on 08-19, and an isolated reading of 42 mg/dL on 08-21 preceded a sensor change. Confirm any unexpected low or high with a fingerstick before acting on it, and follow your usual device and sensor troubleshooting guidance.

The analysis rests on sampled telemetry, 24 of 6214 device statuses and 40 of 2315 treatments, on a non-standard AAPS build with undocumented boost logic, and on an inferred rather than labelled total daily dose. Confidence in the afternoon and overnight conclusions is low, and the proposals should be treated as hypotheses to test under supervision rather than as established findings.
